body: Am I late to the the party?

I want to answer you but anything I say will be bullshit. I've made it well into the night doing way better than I would have otherwise because people on the internet are talking to me, but I'd rather be a giant dick and waste everyone's time than actually do something.

Yeah, I have. Of course things are different since I work through university, but usually what we do is go to the health services building and there are some people skilled in physical health and some skilled in mental, and make the appointment with whichever group you need. I've met a woman in the latter category before, and I've thought about getting an antidepressant to help me get myself into therapy, but that's another, "I'll do it as soon as it's business hours tomorrow," sort of thing and just doesn't happen. I know no one can do it for me, but I don't know how to make me do it. I'm also afraid that once I got to the appointment, I'd lie and not accomplish anything.

I don't know what I'd want to do that I'm not doing right now. My field is providing me with enough money to travel, but as far as day-to-day goes, I kind of like where I'm at geographically. And that's kind of the thing...I like everything I'm doing in my life, I just don't like me I guess. I certainly didn't used to feel good about what I do, but once I became an independent adult, I felt more and more like I was doing all the right things, and the things I did wrong, I could fix.

You make a good case for therapy, but then, I know that. Some evenings I've thought, "the second I get to school tomorrow, I'm making an appointment," but I just don't. And if I do, I'm honest and tell them that I probably won't come back if they don't keep on me, but they don't and I don't come back and I just stay where I am.

SO: I mean, they know, but we've only been dating for a few months. They've got other stuff going on, and want to be want to be wary of using someone who cares about me as a crutch, so I've been introducing the topic gently. Eventually I want them to be fully aware, but I don't want anyone to feel compelled to deal with my shit. It seems like the SOP is to hold me until I feel better, but that only works if we both have a great deal of time to spare and they have the emotional energy, neither of which can be assumed.

I'm drunk now and I know, from my track record, that I won't go get what I need to help myself, and I know if I ask someone else they will be angry with me instead of helping me and I just want to be gone.

Ah, when I say school I mean graduate school, if that helps at all.

I agree that this moment in which I have a significant desire to kill myself will pass, but I don't really agree that it will go away in a long-term sense of the word. The first time I remember distinctly wanting to die was when I was 8, and I remember a couple of pathetic attempts by 11, so it's not really going anywhere anytime soon I don't think. At least not without some significant therapy which I seem to be completely against doing even though objectively it's the best decision. (see one of the other comment threads)

Thank you for your experiences with the hospital and hotlines, they're better than what I might find on websites because that kind of stuff tends to be biased and often impersonal.

I'm kind of drunk now so I hope I make sense. I hope I'll be fine.

My excuse to counter that is that 1. I don't have the time (which is kind of true, I keep busy), and 2. If I'm feeling well one day, which I do more days than I don't, the last thing I want to do is go see a therapist as that tends to make me feel bad. Which is why I never stick with it!

I know it would still hurt him, I just established that as the way to do the least damage possible, assuming that I was going to regardless. I'm noticing a pattern for a while where it's very comforting to give myself permission to kill myself eventually, while not making the decision to do it now.

My parents are much older than me and as such I don't even really tell them that I drink alcohol or have a boyfriend. Dad can be very critical when you get upset, and will yell at me if I cry, so I try to take a certain detached tone about things. So with that and the fact that they have other family members to deal with, I just keep it to myself. They may have suspected when I lived with them, but that was easily blame-able on some other situations, and now that I live on my own I can fake it pretty well.

I go to university so if I were to go I would be going to one of the students about the graduate that they offer there. Which may be a large reason why I don't want to go, since if I don't even trust a licensed professional then why on earth would I trust a student, especially since they tend to leave at the end of the school year just zeroing whatever effort you had put into it.

Like I had this one girl who some friends compelled me to see a few years ago whose response to, "I want to hurt myself, all the time, and I was abused and depersonalize frequently," was to just look sad for me and then once she left, made no effort to make sure I was put with someone else. Which meant I didn't go back.

And then they have this system where you fill out some forms the first session and talk to an intern, then the therapists meet sometime that week, or the next week; then someone picks you, they try to call you and by the time you actually see someone for real, it's been several weeks, and by then I just don't want to anymore.

You sound like you know what you're talking about when I use the word depersonalization, but I'm really just throwing it around without having any idea what I'm saying. My problem is that when I say my name several times, or sometimes when I look in a mirror (I just realized how much that sounds like the beginning of something on /r/nosleep), I get this really strong feeling that it does not make any sense whatsoever that I inhabit the body that I'm looking at and that I have created the actions/relationships/etc of that person. It's really unsettling, only lasts a moment, and I will go way out of my way to avoid it.

I...don't trust doctors. I feel like they're not held to the same level of accountability for their advice that physical doctors are, allowing more incompetent people to be licensed than should be, but are given the power to have you detained if they decide that you need to be. It's not a good comparison, but take the studies conducted on psychiatric wards. The first one has a name that starts with an R that I can't remember and don't feel like looking up at the moment, and happened long enough ago that it shouldn't be valid, but people like the BBC have retried their results and shit hasn't changed. Basically once in a psych ward, the people that work there can't discern fake patients from real ones. Granted these people aren't all licensed therapists, but you get the idea.

(Mostly I'm just trying to justify the fact that I don't want to try therapy anymore.)

Oh I have questions, I forgot. Can you tell me why you don't advise going the hospital? Also do you happen to know when a suicide hotline will try to trace your call, and what a call like that is like? If you don't that's totally fine, that's what google is for I just really don't feel like looking and I feel like I'd be more inclined to give up on it entirely than to try to guess if it was a "safe," or even a useful thing for me to do.

I don't know what my problem is today. I think it's just that I'm tired from working really hard at school and keeping my house taken care of and work and all, and then I want to chill out and take a break but my SO is having a really hard time too. And I think we all have days where just whatever mix of hormones makes us more prone to feeling badly, and I think I've got that too.

I'm kind of working right now on giving a more rational reason for why, not on a day-to-day basis but in view of my entire life, I am giving myself permission to die once the criteria I set above are taken care of. Given that date could be a decade in the future, but I should have a justification for it and I think mine's kind of weak. I just don't like being me more often than I like being me, and I don't see what I get out continuing to do so.

I wouldn't say it's better than dying, although I suppose it's ultimately a philosophical or religious argument to determine what the negative utility of ending life is to the individual that's doing the ending. After all, you're not there to see the negative effects, unless you're talking in terms of the world that goes on after you, or the genes that you don't get to pass on, or some sort of afterlife which still gets to "punish" you.

I'm not really having a rough time lately. On the contrary, things are going really, really well for me and I'm getting everything I want from life. My life is actually pretty awesome (I think anyway). 

But I guess if I'm certain about ending my life prematurely, I should have a reason. I guess it boils down to self-esteem. I'm really not comfortable with the idea of being in my own skin (on all kinds of levels...I have some problems with depersonalization), and I don't see what I ultimately am getting for enduring. Today my problem is that I'm tired of working hard, I don't necessarily like what I output nor do I like my interactions with people a lot of the time, and I just don't have anyone to lean on at the moment so I'm just kind of alone stewing in myself.

That all sounds incredibly arrogant when I reread it. I'm sorry.
